Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2590; barren (literally or figuratively):--without fruit, unfruitful.
BiblicalUsage: The word is barren, without fruit. The seed among thorns is choked and becometh unfruitful; Paul says to have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness; and Peter says that if grace's virtues abound in us, they will keep us from being barren nor unfruitful. The picture is a tree that takes up ground and gives nothing back.
TheologicalSignificance: Fruit is the test Jesus Himself set. I believe this word is a warning to every comfortable Christian: a life with leaves and no fruit is not a growing life, and the cure Peter names is not trying harder but abounding in the graces God gives.
RelatedTopics: Fruit of the Spirit; Growth; Discipleship
